name: PETG (Glycol-Modified PET)
chemical_makeup: Polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified — a copolyester of PET in which cyclohexanedimethanol (CHDM) replaces part of the ethylene glycol, suppressing crystallisation to give an amorphous, tough, easily printed polymer
summary: The workhorse step up from PLA: tougher, far better layer adhesion, genuinely water-resistant and usable to ~70 °C, with only mild warp and no enclosure requirement. Pays for it with stringing, oozing, softer detail and supports that fuse hard to the part.

printing.notes: Prusa profiles run 230 °C first layer / 240 °C for the rest; the Prusament TDS quotes 250±10 °C. Keep part cooling low — fan off for the first layers, then roughly half power; heavy cooling is the main cause of brittle, poorly bonded PETG. No chamber needed, but a draft-free room (or an enclosure on large parts) helps. Hardened nozzle only for CF/GF-filled PETG.

feeding.notes: Listed AMS-compatible by Bambu and unproblematic in Prusa's MMU: rigid, non-abrasive and only moderately hygroscopic. The exception is CF/GF-filled PETG from third parties, which is barred because the fibres abrade the AMS PTFE tubes. Enclosure: Bambu's heat-creep table and QIDI's door-open table both keep the cover installed for PETG, so enclosure_open_for_cooling is false — PETG's Tg is high enough that chamber heat helps rather than hurts, though Bambu does note PETG can suffer heat creep if the enclosure runs unusually hot.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/hissing or steam at the nozzle tip; glossy rather than foggy or matte extrudate; markedly reduced stringing; no surface bubbles or voids in the extruded strand
drying.notes: Prusa recommends 55 °C for 6 h, Bambu 65 °C for 8 h; heavily soaked spools may need 6-10 h. Do not exceed ~65-70 °C — spools deform. Wet PETG bubbles and hydrolyses visibly, so drying is effectively routine rather than occasional.

storage.recommendations: Sealed container or drybox with desiccant; re-absorbs moisture noticeably faster than PLA, so store it sealed between prints rather than only before them

price.notes: 2025-2026 pricing for standard unfilled grades: budget $18-22, mid $22-26, premium $30-42 per kg. The historical price gap with ABS has closed — budget PETG now often matches or undercuts ABS.

recommended: outdoor brackets and enclosures (moderate UV exposure)
water bottles and non-potable liquid containment
parts where layer adhesion / Z-strength is critical
not_recommended: high-precision dimensional parts (more ooze and stringing than PLA)
parts with crisp overhangs or long bridges (sags and droops)
geometry needing easy support removal (supports fuse strongly)
fine-detail miniatures (glossy, stringy finish blurs detail)

properties.notes: Prusament PETG measures HDT 68 °C and yield ~46-50 MPa; Polymaker PolyLite PETG reports 50.8 MPa and partmfg.com 52.2 MPa. Tg is not on the Prusament TDS; secondary sources put it at 80-85 °C. Max service temp is an estimate, not a datasheet value.

compatibility.notes: Welds cleanly to itself and to PCTG (same copolyester family); some TPU formulations bond to PETG but the weld is weaker than a same-family joint, so treat flex/rigid PETG-TPU as semi-compatible only. Does not weld to PLA — deliberately, so PLA makes a clean breakaway support for PETG and vice versa. BVOH is the soluble support of choice (PVA pairs better with PLA). PETG plus ABS/ASA is not a standard combination: the chemistry, nozzle windows and warp behaviour clash even though bed temperatures overlap.

plate_recommendations.notes: Textured/satin or powder-coated PEI is the right surface for PETG at 70-90 °C bed. On SMOOTH PEI, always apply a glue stick as a separator — bare PETG bonds so hard it can tear the coating off the sheet on removal.

emissions.notes: No styrene, and odour is mild. Azimi et al. (2016) placed PET-based filament (T-Glase) around 5×10⁹ particles/min — above PLA but well below ABS, PC and HIPS; a precise figure for generic PETG is unverified. Ventilation is optional for occasional open-air printing and recommended for long or enclosed jobs.

safety_notes: Carbon- and glass-filled PETG grades are abrasive and require a hardened nozzle; fibre dust from sanding filled grades should not be inhaled.
additional_notes: Base PETG resin is used for injection-moulded food packaging and some filament lines are sold as food-contact certified, but a printed part's layer crevices and unverified nozzle/additive contamination mean an FDM PETG part is not food-safe without sealing or single-use handling.

provenance.conflicts: HDT: Prusament measures 68 °C while other property tables cite 78-80 °C — recorded as 72 °C with the 68-80 °C spread noted. Hygroscopy: the Prusament TDS reports only 0.07-0.10 % moisture uptake at 7 days for that formulation, while field consensus classes bulk PETG as a moderate-to-high absorber needing routine drying — 'moderate' recorded. Shrinkage: some sources place PETG slightly below PLA, others slightly above. The particulate figure is extrapolated from a PET-based filament (T-Glase), not measured for generic PETG.
